STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits well below the rim with a curved inner wall visible on all sides, so this is a shallow-to-medium salad bowl.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: a salad bowl is typically 20-25 cm wide.
b) Reference: the avocado slices are about 9-10 cm long and the bowl spans roughly 2.3-2.5 avocado lengths across, giving about 22-24 cm. The olives (~2.5 cm) lying across the bowl also suggest a bowl of about 22 cm.
Reconciled width: 23 cm.

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Chicken (diced, grilled): visible cubes cover roughly 35% of the surface. Estimated mass from volume: a fill-based estimate for the whole salad is below.
- Avocado: 4 wedges/slices visible, roughly 1 whole avocado portion, about 100-120 g.
- Spinach/leafy greens: raw, covering most of the bowl, loose leaves 3-5 cm deep. Bowl capacity = 0.2 x 23^3 / 1000 ≈ 2.4 l for a shallow bowl. Fill ≈ 0.6 (food sits below rim). Food volume = 2.4 x 0.6 x 0.6 ≈ 0.86 l = 860 ml. Greens share ~55%: 470 ml x 0.15 = about 70 g.
- Chicken share ~25%: 215 ml x 1.0 = about 215 g... this is high for the visible pieces, so I reduce to a more realistic ~120 g since the cubes are sparse and the bowl's fill is partly leaves.
- Black olives (or kalamata-style olives), about 8 visible: 8 x 4 g = 32 g, plus a few hidden, ~40 g.
- Avocado: ~110 g.

Final item grams (rounded): spinach 70 g, grilled chicken 120 g, avocado 110 g, olives 40 g. Total ≈ 340 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: the greens form the base, already included. No additional hidden layer is evident.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Raw spinach: 23 kcal
- Grilled chicken breast: 165 kcal
- Avocado: 160 kcal
- Black olives: 115 kcal

Energy: spinach 70 g = 16 kcal; chicken 120 g = 198 kcal; avocado 110 g = 176 kcal; olives 40 g = 46 kcal. Total ≈ 436 kcal.
